explanations.explanation_right_atrium: The right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the body through the superior and inferior venae cavae.
explanations.explanation_right_ventricle: The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood into the pulmonary trunk and on to the lungs.
explanations.explanation_left_atrium: The left atrium receives oxygenated blood returning from the lungs through the pulmonary veins.
explanations.explanation_left_ventricle: The left ventricle has the thickest muscle wall. It pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta and around the whole body.
explanations.explanation_aorta: The aorta is the largest artery. Its arch gives off branches to the head and arms before it runs down through the body.
explanations.explanation_pulmonary_trunk: The pulmonary trunk carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle and splits into the left and right pulmonary arteries.
explanations.explanation_superior_vena_cava: The superior vena cava returns deoxygenated blood from the head, neck and arms to the right atrium.
explanations.explanation_inferior_vena_cava: The inferior vena cava returns deoxygenated blood from the lower body to the right atrium.
explanations.explanation_pulmonary_veins: Four pulmonary veins bring oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium.
explanations.explanation_coronary_arteries: The coronary arteries branch from the base of the aorta and supply the heart muscle itself. A blockage here causes a heart attack.
explanations.explanation_cardiac_veins: Cardiac veins drain used blood from the heart muscle into the coronary sinus, which empties into the right atrium.
